citeAs: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091.
creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
description: The Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark evaluates the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to recognize conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts evenly distributed between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, spanning 8 tasks. It is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework (AutoCreate) that leverages programs and large language models, and includes three splits: SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%).
name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark - self-contradictory variant
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: LLM evaluation agents were validated against human expert evaluations. Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were calculated between LLM agent and human expert evaluations on vision-language conflicts: GPT-4V replies: Spearman's ρ=0.881, Concordance=94%; LLaVA-1.5 replies: Spearman's ρ=0.999, Concordance=99%; Gemini replies: Spearman's ρ=0.854, Concordance=97%. GPT-4 was found to closely align with human evaluative standards.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts manually checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. For evaluation, human experts evaluated replies from LMMs to determine whether they successfully identified conflicts. A uniform prompt for all tasks was designed to prompt LLMs as evaluation agents. Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were calculated to measure evaluation consistency between humans and LLM agents (GPT-4 showed Spearman's ρ of 0.881 with 94% concordance for GPT-4V replies; LLaVA-1.5 showed 0.999 with 99%; Gemini showed 0.854 with 97%).
rai:dataBiases: The dataset uses synthetic/automatically generated data via LLMs, which may introduce biases inherent to the LLMs used for generation. SemanticConflict relies on ImageNet, which has known class distribution and demographic biases. The paper notes that LLM-generated questions may have ambiguous answers even with explicit emphasis on uniqueness, requiring an LLM agent to filter them.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using AutoCreate, a novel automatic dataset creation framework that leverages programs and large language models (LLMs). AutoCreate starts from a small batch of manually input seeds and automatically generates large quantities of high-quality, diverse data through iterative cycles. Each cycle includes a Language Loop and a Visual Loop, each processed by a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. For SemanticConflict, images are retrieved from the ImageNet dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) manually crafted seed prompts and instruction pairs; (2) LLM-generated texts (contexts, questions, descriptions, fictional objects); (3) programmatically generated images (OCR images with varying fonts/sizes/colors, bar/pie/line charts, geometric shape images); (4) ImageNet dataset images (for SemanticConflict, using the imagenet-1k validation set).
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: Only language-language and vision-language paradigms are included; more modalities will be added in future work. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. No detailed study is provided on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, the data dictionary is tampered with by changing the largest value to the smallest value before plotting. For GeometricConflict, two attributes in the text description are exchanged to introduce confusion. For SemanticConflict, the correct class label in questions is substituted with a similar but different object. For OCRConflict, images vary in font, size, and color to augment diversity. For FigureConflict, charts are plotted with random choices for font, size, color, and other style options.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A Cleaner component in AutoCreate removes data that does not meet quality standards. Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. For SCI-Core and SCI-Base, subsets are selected manually with sizes of 1% and 10% of SCI-All respectively. For ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, and OCRConflict, extra effort is applied to guarantee diversity when used in SCI-Core. An LLM agent is used to judge whether generated questions have unique answers (for ForbbidenConflict).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCI benchmark provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. The CaP approach integrates external cognition into multimodal models, enhancing context-aware understanding. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration. The benchmark also addresses challenges for language beginners and vulnerable populations who may not recognize multimodal conflicts.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect and recognize self-contradictory or conflicting instructions in both language-language and vision-language paradigms. Benchmarking LMM performance on instruction conflict detection. Assessing prompting strategies (zero-shot, chain-of-thought, few-shot, self-consistency, Cognitive Awakening Prompting) for improving dissonance detection in LMMs.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) were used throughout the AutoCreate pipeline for: generating seed data, creating conflicting instructions, generating object descriptions, extracting attribute descriptions, generating contradictory sentences, generating questions, and quality-checking (judging uniqueness of answers). GPT-4 was used as an evaluation agent to assess whether LMM replies identified conflicts. ImageNet was used as a source for SemanticConflict images.
